documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
47M yearly physical.

Since last year: two stones, R in June 2024 and L in December, both passed after ED visits; nothing since December. Keeping water up most weekdays. HTN on HCTZ 25 without trouble.

Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Never smoker, drinks rarely. PHQ-2 0.

ROS: negative, specifically no flank pain, hematuria, abdominal pain or change in bowel habits.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, well. HEENT normal. Neck without masses. Heart RRR, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft and nontender with healed old RLQ incision. No CVA tenderness. Extremities warm, no edema. Skin normal.

A/P
- Annual labs: CMP, lipids, A1c, and a UA.
- FIT kit, third year.
- Flu shot at a nurse visit in October.
- HTN controlled. Continue.
- Stones: continue fluids and diet changes.

Return for BP check in spring, physical next September.

conditions.note: adhesive small bowel obstruction after 2013 open appendectomy

reports.text: Upright view of the abdomen. Multiple dilated loops of small bowel with air-fluid levels. No free intraperitoneal air beneath the diaphragm. Osseous structures unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Findings consistent with small bowel obstruction. No free air.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, general surgery service. Admitted 11/26/2025, discharged 11/30/2025.

Reason for admission: adhesive small bowel obstruction.

History: 47M with HTN on HCTZ and recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis with prior ureteral stones. Several days of worsening abdominal discomfort and eating little, then no stool or flatus since the day before admission and 12 hours of diffuse cramping pain, bloating and repeated vomiting. Denied fever, hematemesis, melena, bright red blood or urinary symptoms. Prior open appendectomy for a perforated appendix about 12 years ago. NKDA.

On arrival: T 37.3, BP 104/68, HR 112, RR 22. Uncomfortable and mildly dry. Abdomen distended with high-pitched bowel sounds throughout, diffusely tender, no rebound or guarding. Rectal exam unremarkable.
Upright abdominal film: dilated small bowel loops with air-fluid levels, no free air.

Diagnoses: adhesive small bowel obstruction; dehydration.

Course: managed nonoperatively. NPO, nasogastric tube to suction, IV fluids. HCTZ held. Tachycardia settled with fluids. Flatus returned hospital day 3 (11/28); NG removed, diet advanced over 2 days. Tolerating regular diet with bowel movement before discharge. No operation.

Discharge meds: resume hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Instructions: small meals for a few days, return for vomiting, distension or inability to pass gas. Follow up with PCP in 1 week.

documents.title: Patient call from hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called from his hospital room. Admitted Wednesday for a bowel blockage, surgery team says it's scar tissue from his old appendix operation. Has had a tube in his nose and IV fluids, no surgery so far. Passed gas this morning and they're talking about taking the tube out. Wanted us to know. Told him we'll see him after discharge; he'll call when he's home. Message to PCP.

conditions.label: Intestinal adhesions [bands], unspecified as to partial versus complete obstruction

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Summary not yet received; history from patient and his discharge instruction sheet.

Admitted 11/26 to 11/30 with an adhesive small bowel obstruction, adhesions from the 2013 open appendectomy. Treated with NG tube, bowel rest and fluids, no surgery. Told he was dehydrated on arrival. HCTZ was held in the hospital and he restarted it 12/1 per the sheet.

Now: eating regular meals, smaller portions. BMs daily, normal. No pain, no bloating, no vomiting. Back at work Monday. Drinking well.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP in his usual range. Looks well. Abdomen soft, nondistended, nontender, normal bowel sounds, incision healed.

A/P
1. Adhesive SBO, resolved without surgery. Reviewed warning signs: crampy pain with bloating, vomiting, no gas. Go straight to the ED if it recurs.
2. Dehydration, resolved. BMP today after the vomiting and IV fluids, and back on the thiazide.
3. HTN: continue HCTZ 25.

Will request the discharge summary.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: BMP normal, electrolytes and kidney function back to baseline. Portal message sent to patient.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at his desk at work, identity confirmed.

BP check. Bought a home cuff after the hospital stay. Sent a photo of his log: two weeks of morning readings mostly in the high 120s to low 130s over low 80s. No symptoms. Taking HCTZ daily.
No abdominal pain or bloating since December, bowels normal. No flank pain.

Assessment: HTN at goal on home readings. Continue HCTZ 25. Office visit with labs in late summer, physical in the fall.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: BP follow-up, 48 now. Home log still 120s-130s/80s. On HCTZ 25 daily, no side effects. No stone episodes since 12/2024. No abdominal symptoms since the obstruction last November. Summer heat at the warehouse, says he's been good about water.

O: vitals as charted. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.

A/P
1. HTN controlled. Continue hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. BMP today.
2. Recurrent nephrolithiasis: quiet, continue fluids.
3. Lipids today since we're drawing anyway.

Physical booked for September; will refill HCTZ when the labs are back.

documents.title: Lab results from Wednesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Adam, everything from Wednesday's draw looks normal: potassium, sodium, kidney function, calcium and cholesterol. Keep going with the hydrochlorothiazide.

documents.body: Thanks for the results. I'm down to about a week of the water pill, can you send the refill to the same pharmacy?

documents.body: Done, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg 90-day supply with 3 refills went to your pharmacy this morning. See you at your physical in September.
